title: Surreal rate calculus — infinitesimal setup and classical-limit rate table
html:
Remark. Surreal rate calculus — infinitesimal setup and classical-limit rate table

Let \varepsilon \in \mathrm{Der}(A) be the Reeb infinitesimal (Reeb infinitesimal) and let q = 1 + \varepsilon (q from \varepsilon) be the associated substrate parameter. Work inside the ordered field \mathbb{R}(\varepsilon) of rational functions of \varepsilon, and treat \varepsilon as a strictly positive infinitesimal: for every standard real \lambda > 0 and every n \in \mathbb{N}, n \cdot \varepsilon < \lambda.

Equivalently, via the surreal appendix (calculus up to \varepsilon, surreal blow-up calculus), \varepsilon = 1 / \omega inside Conway's surreal field \mathbf{No}. The asymptotic symbols \asymp, O(\cdot), o(\cdot), \Theta(\cdot) below are the surreal-valuation forms of Big-O surreal — equality up to a standard-real prefactor (for \asymp) or leading-exponent comparison (for the others).

Rate table. Each scaling law of the classical-limit degenerations of collapse of the quantum gap has a literal value as an element of \mathbb{R}(\varepsilon) \subset \mathbf{No}:

Classical-limit quantity Surreal value Order in \varepsilon
Mass gap \Delta_q of the q-Laplacian \asymp \tfrac{1}{2}\,\varepsilon^3 +3 (positive infinitesimal)
Reeb period \Omega_q \asymp \varepsilon^{-1} -1 (positive transfinite)
Enstrophy ceiling (fluid-dynamics \S 3) \asymp \varepsilon^{-4/3} -4/3 (transfinite)
Rogue-zero energy cost E(\delta) for standard \delta > 0 \asymp \delta^2 \cdot \varepsilon^{-1} -1 (transfinite scaled by \delta^2)

Here \asymp means "equal up to a strictly positive standard-real prefactor", so the order of each quantity in \varepsilon is an invariant of the substrate, independent of normalization conventions.
